items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And then Doug Hammond came in with a tape. He had talked to Charles Tolliver and Charles Tolliver didn’t have time at that particular time. I said well I’ll give you some time, man, give me the tape and I’ll listen to it. And it was good.

ctx.x: Okay. So I started up again. Let me ask you about Tribe. Would bands come to you, groups of musicians, with a finished audio recording and then you would take that and put it out on your label? Or did you work with the musicians from the get-go?

No, well I was working with a cadre of musicians. I was working with Phil Ranelin, which we started a partnership, Tribe Records. The magazine was different. But I needed some help on administrative stuff so I incorporated with Phil and myself as Tribe Records. And then Marcus — I used Marcus Belgrave and Harold McKinney basically was the network. Because we was playing in each other’s group. I was playing in Marcus’s group, me and Phil was playing in Marcus’s group, was playing in Harold’s group, you know, and…

groove. And then a guy from Ann Arbor, Ron Brooks submitted some music and David Durrah out of Cleveland submitted some music. So anyway that’s how that started, and then we distributed this music by independent distributors that was happening all over America, independent distributors, they wanted to distribute their own product and have their own catalogue as opposed to working for Atlantic Records or a big corporation. This was like an independent revolution as it were, you know, in the 60s. Everybody was…

items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: A box of Harold, Doug. So I’m selling a catalogue and they’re picking things off the catalogue.

ctx.x: I’m sorry, some of this music made its way over to Europe, didn’t it?

The first big marketplace we hit was Poland. Poland. The Czech Republic. You know they’re the ones that did the big write-up in a magazine talking about the label and talking about the first three different releases and whatnot. Then Germany, then France and Spain and eventually Japan, Australia you know. But we had 15 distributors at that time that was ordering. I was mainly selling myself, because I was excited, excited. Then I had other people that helped me out, but I got it started myself. I would contact…

distributors myself and started packaging these records and taking orders. After we had sent everything out to the radio stations and the magazines and newspapers was writing articles, then I would get on the telephone and talk about how the records was being covered and it’s being reviewed and radio stations is playing it, it’s in rotation and blah- blah-blah-blah. And then the distributors would say, “Well send me a box.” And a box was like 25. And then, next month they want two boxes. You know, of each. I’m…
